message:
Fix Windows crash: request int64 explicitly in LegacyNumpyRandom.randint

On Windows, RandomState.randint defaults to the C long, which is 32 bits
there and 64 bits on Linux. losses.py:_sample_patch_points asks for a
64-bit seed, so the fit dies at the first optimizer iteration with
"ValueError: high is out of bounds for int32".

This is the default path, not an edge case: prefetch_enabled() returns
False unless FIT_SPIRAL_PREFETCH=1 is set. The prefetch path is fine,
because its rng is a _GeneratorShim delegating to Generator.integers,
whose default dtype is int64. The shim takes no dtype argument, so the
fix belongs in LegacyNumpyRandom rather than in losses.py.

int64 is requested only when the bound does not fit in int32, so every
existing small-range call keeps the exact historical bit stream, which
is the stated purpose of this class.

Also fixes the same latent pitfall in StepPrefetcher.np_rng.

Simplify to a two-line change, one per call site

Requested by review: drop the conditional and the explanatory comment,
and always request int64.

The conditional was not load bearing. Measured on Windows, where the
default integer type is int32, the drawn stream is identical with and
without dtype=int64 across 77 bound and seed combinations. The shorter
form is also a better drop in: it still accepts an array bound, which
the previous int(bound) narrowed to scalars only.
